term.description: Ontology term for the category as a CURIE.

Channel.description: The base channel. Every channel, whatever its type, MUST be valid as a base channel. Readers that do not recognise `type` MUST treat the channel as a base channel and MUST ignore attributes they do not know. Writers MUST NOT put rendering attributes (colour, window, lookup table) on a channel.

component.description: Membership of a colour image stored as separate planes.

description.description: Free-text description of the channel for humans and language models.

entities.description: What the channel reports on, each with its role.

id.description: Identifier of the channel, unique for the multiscale. Other metadata (rendering, biological annotation, statistics, transformations) references the channel by this id. Follows the RFC-8 id pattern; UUIDs are allowed but not required.

name.description: Human-readable name of the channel. It MUST be unique within the `channels` list, so that a channel can be looked up by name.

provenance.description: Whether the channel was acquired, derived or simulated, and from what.

quantity.description: What the stored values measure. This attribute is OPTIONAL. When absent, values are intensities in arbitrary units.

terms.description: Ontology terms for the channel as a whole, e.g. an imaging-method term, as CURIEs. Prefixes SHOULD follow bioregistry.io.

type.description: The channel type: one of the core types (fluorescence, optical, electron, scanning_probe, spectroscopic, diffraction, xray, computed), "generic", or an extension type given as a namespaced http(s) URI. Typed subclasses pin this value with equals_string; other values are invalid.

Channel.title: Channel

Component.description: Channels with the same `group` together form one colour image. A group MUST contain each component of its colour model exactly once.

group.description: Identifier shared by the channels of one colour image.

Component.title: Component

Entity.description: Something the channel reports on. The same roles apply across domains: a DAPI channel (DAPI, DNA, nucleus), an imaging mass cytometry channel (165Ho, CD3, T cell) and an EDS map (iron in a steel matrix).

term.description: Ontology or database term for the entity as a CURIE. Prefixes SHOULD follow bioregistry.io.

Entity.title: Entity

method.description: Short description of, or URI for, the method that produced the channel.

sources.description: Ids of the channels this channel was derived from. Channels in other documents will be referenced with RFC-8 References once RFC-8 is settled.

Quantity.description: The physical quantity the stored values represent and how to calibrate them. The calibration applies to pixel values, not to coordinates, and is unrelated to RFC-5 scale transformations.

categories.description: For categorical channels such as EBSD phase maps or classifier outputs, a map from stored value to the category it stands for, serialized as { "<stored value>": { "name": ..., "term": ... } }.

name.description: The measured quantity, e.g. intensity, counts, height, phase, potential, force, modulus, lifetime, probability, angle, concentration. Values from the recommended vocabulary SHOULD be used; other values are allowed.

unit.description: Unit of the physical value, spelled as for axes (e.g. nanometer, volt, degree, nanosecond). This attribute is OPTIONAL; if it is absent, the values are in arbitrary units.

value_offset.description: Linear calibration, physical = stored * value_scale + value_offset. Defaults to 0.

value_scale.description: Linear calibration, physical = stored * value_scale + value_offset. Defaults to 1.
